title: Protocol for the generation of Symbiodiniaceae mutants using UV mutagenesis
author: Russo, Xiang, et al.
materials: Class II type A2 biosafety cabinet

Timing: ∼2 h
9.Place a large metal paper clip (approximately 47 mm in length) on the inside of each empty glass Petri dish (7 total, or as many needed for each time point) and wrap the Petri dishes in aluminum foil for autoclaving.10.Autoclave at 121°C for 30 min.

steps.title: Prepare sterile liquid MB media
steps.instruction: Add 37.4 g MB media mix per liter ultrapure water, autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min, cool to 22 °C, then filter through a sterile 0.22‑µm vacuum system to remove precipitated particles.

substeps.instruction: Add MB mix to ultrapure water (37.4 g L⁻¹)
Filter sterile 0.22 µm to eliminate precipitate

steps.title: Set incubator conditions for axenic cultures
steps.instruction: Program the incubator to 27 °C with a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle and a light intensity of 5–10 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ PAR.

steps.title: Prepare liquid pre‑cultures from axenic colonies
steps.instruction: In at least three 50 mL flasks add 25 mL sterile liquid MB, inoculate each with cells from a single axenic colony on agar, and incubate under the set conditions for 2–3 weeks until cell density reaches ~1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Generate growth‑curve flasks
steps.instruction: For each pre‑culture, aliquot 1.5 × 10⁷ cells into a sterile 50 mL tube, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, resuspend pellet in 1 mL sterile MB, add 74 mL sterile MB and the 1 mL cell suspension to a sterilized 250 mL flask to obtain 2 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹; prepare at least three such flasks, record cell concentration every 4–5 days, and stop when stationary phase is observed (no change for two consecutive measurements).

substeps.instruction: Add 74 mL sterile MB + 1 mL suspension to 250 mL flask (final 2 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹)
Stop when stationary phase (no change two consecutive points)

steps.title: Scale up cultures for mutagenesis
steps.instruction: Repeat the growth‑curve procedure to obtain three pre‑cultures with ≥1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹; from each, take 1.5 × 10⁷ cells, centrifuge, resuspend in 5 mL fresh MB, transfer to a sterilized 250 mL flask containing 70 mL MB to reach 2 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹, grow to 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, then propagate as described until log phase ≥2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ before UV treatment.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge and resuspend in 5 mL fresh MB
Transfer to 250 mL flask with 70 mL MB (final 2 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹)
Propagate to log phase ≥2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹

steps.title: Prepare solid MB agar with glucose
steps.instruction: For 1 L, combine MB media mix, glucose to 0.5 g L⁻¹, and agar to 1.5 % w/v in ultrapure water, autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min, then cool to 60–70 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add MB mix, 0.5 g L⁻¹ glucose, 1.5 % w/v agar to water (1 L total)

steps.title: Dispense agar into Petri dishes and dry
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, dispense 24 mL of the cooled agar into each 100 mm × 15 mm plastic Petri dish while avoiding precipitated particles; then turn off the biosafety cabinet and let the plates dry for 12 h with the sash down.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 24 mL agar per 100 mm × 15 mm dish
Dry plates 12 h in biosafety cabinet (sash down)

steps.title: Prepare paper‑clip equipment for UV plates
steps.instruction: Place a metal paper clip approximately 47 mm long inside each empty glass Petri dish (seven dishes or as many as needed for the experiment) and wrap the dishes in aluminum foil for autoclaving.

substeps.instruction: Insert ~47 mm metal paper clip into each glass dish

steps.title: Autoclave paper‑clip equipped dishes
steps.instruction: Autoclave the foil‑wrapped dishes at 121 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Establish UV exposure survival curve
steps.instruction: Expose test plates to a range of UV doses, count surviving colonies, plot survival, and select an exposure that yields ≤1 % survival for mutant generation.

steps.title: Primary screen for mutant phenotypes
steps.instruction: Choose a phenotypic trait, inspect colonies from the selected UV‑exposure plate with a dissection microscope, and identify candidate mutants based on visual differences.

steps.title: Isolate candidate mutants onto fresh media
steps.instruction: In a sterile environment, prepare a solid‑media plate or a 96‑well plate with 200 µL MB liquid per well; using a sterilized toothpick, transfer cells from each candidate colony to the destination plate, ensuring attachment and avoiding off‑target cells, then streak onto fresh solid media or inoculate liquid media.

substeps.instruction: Prepare solid plate or 96‑well plate (200 µL MB per well)
Streak onto fresh solid media or inoculate liquid media

steps.title: Grow isolated mutants for recovery
steps.instruction: Incubate the transferred mutants under permissive conditions for at least 1 month to allow recovery and verify viability before downstream use.

steps.title: Secondary screen to confirm phenotype
steps.instruction: Create 2–3 backup copies of each putative mutant (streak onto separate solid plates or transfer 30 µL into a fresh 170 µL liquid well), maintain by monthly transfers, grow mutants and the original Breviolum minutum strain side‑by‑side under comparable conditions that highlight the phenotype for ~1 month, then assess whether the expected phenotypic change is present.

substeps.instruction: Make 2–3 backup copies (solid plates or 30 µL → 170 µL liquid)
Grow mutant and original strain together under comparable conditions for ~1 month

steps.title: Propagate and maintain validated mutants
steps.instruction: Continue culturing mutants that show the confirmed phenotype, keeping the original strain on the same plate for comparison; repeat UV mutagenesis if needed, adjusting nutrients, lighting, or temperature (e.g., heterotrophic dark growth with dextrose for photosynthesis‑deficient mutants). Aim for ~1000 surviving colonies per plate to ensure successful isolation.
